transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Skyward Head of ML), Evan Cole (Skyward Platform Eng), Marcus Li (CTO)

Summary (auto):
- Customer evaluating whether to start on Hosted and move to Dedicated or go Private directly for sensitive data.
- Key requirements: long context / 32k for legal docs, strong multilingual (EN/ES/DE/JA), tool-calling into internal vector DB and ticketing system, SOC2+KMS.
- Next steps: pricing sheet, benchmark configs, SE-led technical deep-dive.

Topics: model selection, context length, multilingual, tool-calling, compliance (SOC2/KMS), hosting options

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena: Hi everyone good to see you. Thanks for taking the time. I'm Lena from Redwood, account exec. Carlos from our SE team is on, he'll do the deeper technical bits.
[00:07] Priya: Hi thanks Lena. We are Priya, head of ml at Skyward, with Evan and Marcus. We wanted to focus today on model selection — we have a mix of product-use cases and sensitive client PII so we wanted to get a sense of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs.
[00:22] Marcus: Also multilingual support is a must, and for some of our legal ingestion we need up to 32k token context.
[00:30] Carlos: Great thanks. I'll try to map our model catalog and deployment modes to those requirements. Quick qualification: are you leaning towards open models vs closed commercial models? Any pre-existing vendor preferences?
[00:42] Evan: We tried some prototypes with OpenAI but cost and data residency are concerns. We're interested in open models that we can run on Dedicated or Private but we'd like to know how Redwood's Hosted catalog compares.
[00:55] Priya: And tool-calling — we need the model to call our vector DB and also trigger structured calls to our ticketing system for suggested triage. How does Redwood support that?
[01:08] Carlos: We have streaming responses and function/tool calling support in the API; for Hosted we offer managed tool-calling integrations and webhooks, for Dedicated/Private you can run the tool-caller inside your VPC and we support secure outbound calls or an event-sink pattern. There can be slight differences in latency depending on routing.
[01:28] Priya: Are there any limitations on model features for open models in Hosted vs Dedicated? For example support for longer context windows, kv-cache, or quantized runtimes?
[01:38] Carlos: Good q. Hosted exposes tuned variants of open models — we currently have 8k, 16k and 32k context variants for some models. On Dedicated you can pin specific variants and we support quantized runtimes (q4_0, q8_0) to reduce cost. For Private deployments we ship the runtime and you can tune kernels/quantization locally, but obviously that takes more ops.
[01:58] Marcus: For the 32k variant — is that native or stitched / sliding window? We need coherent attention for long legal docs.
[02:06] Carlos: For the 32k we use attention kernels optimized for long sequences; it's native in the sense that the model weights are the long-context flavor. For extremely long docs we still recommend prefix KV caching and summarization pipelines but customers have run coherent full-document passes at 32k.
[02:21] Priya: Nice. Latency implications? We're latency-sensitive for interactive agents.
[02:25] Carlos: Latency does increase roughly linearly with sequence length at generation time. For interactive UIs you can pick a smaller context window for immediate responses and use background reranking or retrieval-augmented summaries. Dedicated offers lower P99s because of reserved GPU capacity and you can also choose faster kernels/higher-memory GPUs. Hosted is great for quick onboarding but dedicated gives predictable tail latency.
[02:45] Evan: On the security front we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, and detailed audit logs. Hosted can we do customer-managed keys?
[02:55] Lena: Hosted supports KMS integrations for enterprise accounts; there are options for bringing your own key in some regions. For the most strict KMS/air-gap needs, Private is the better fit. We also have audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM.
[03:12] Marcus: What about data retention in Hosted? We don't want anything persisted longer than 30 days and must ensure PII handling.
[03:18] Lena: We can set retention policies and role-based access for logs; for maximum control Dedicated isolates your workloads and Private gives you full control over storage. We'll include our data retention docs in the follow-up.
[03:30] Priya: Let's talk models — which open models would you recommend for multilingual and tool-calling? Spanish and German are our heavy ones, and we also do Japanese.
[03:40] Carlos: For multilingual, some of the newer open models are strong (Mistral-ish and Llama2/3 variants). We have Redwood-curated variants that are tuned for multilingual quality. For tool-calling it's more about the inference runtime and tokenization; we ensure function calling is supported across our catalog, but the model's instruction-following quality matters — we can share evals.
[04:01] Priya: Any tradeoffs between instruction tuned closed models vs open model tuned variants?
[04:06] Carlos: Closed models tend to have stronger OOTB instruction behavior, but tuned open models can get very close and give you more deployment flexibility (Dedicated/Private). Also open models are easier to quantize for cost. It's a trade between immediate quality and long-term control/TCO.
[04:21] Evan: On quantization — we're interested in q4_0 and q8_0. Does Redwood's runtime support these and what's the impact on latency/quality?
[04:31] Carlos: Yes runtime supports q4_0 and q8_0 paths. q4_0 gives big memory savings but may have small quality regressions on some tasks; q8_0 is a middle ground. We'll share benchmark numbers and recommend per-workload profiles. On Dedicated you can choose GPU types that make q4_0 latency favorable.
[04:49] Priya: One more: tool-calling into our vector DB — we want the model to retrieve docs and then call functions to triage. How does Redwood manage the security of those function calls?
[04:59] Carlos: For Hosted we proxy function calls through a secure webhook with HMAC and audit logs; for Dedicated/Private we can run the tool caller in your VPC so calls never leave your network. We also support token exchange and short-lived creds for downstream systems.
[05:14] Marcus: Good. On benchmarking: can we run a quick A/B between an open 32k hosted variant and a dedicated pinned model with q4_0 to compare latency and tokens cost?
[05:24] Lena: Absolutely. Carlos will propose a simple benchmark harness and we can run a small pilot.
[05:29] Priya: Timeline question — we have an RFP in June, would like a pilot before June 15 if possible. Is that feasible?
[05:36] Lena: Yes, we can try to scope a 2-week pilot to show latency/cost and quality. We'll aim to have configs and pricing in the next 2 business days.
[05:45] Evan: Regarding multilingual regen — do you ship per-language fine-tuning or do you recommend retrieval augmentation?
[05:52] Carlos: Usually retrieval augmentation + prompt templates are cheaper and faster. Per-language fine-tuning offered but it's more involved; we can discuss based on sample evals you send.
[05:59] Priya: Ok. Can you also share any redwood-verified performance profiles for the models so our infra team can preplan GPU sizing for Dedicated?
[06:07] Carlos: Yes, we'll share per-model throughput/latency tables, memory footprints, and recommended GPU types.
[06:14] Marcus: One operational question: how do rollouts work if we pin a model version? Can we do canary and automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated capacity is saturated?
[06:24] Carlos: Yes, our routing layer supports policies: you can set a primary endpoint (Dedicated) and fallback to Hosted variants automatically. Canary and A/B are supported as well.
[06:33] Priya: Great. A few random Qs from Evan — what's the SDK support, do you have Python/Go/JS clients?
[06:39] Lena: We have official SDKs for Python and JS, and REST for Go. Also a CLI for deployments.
[06:45] Evan: For observability, we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency.
[06:50] Carlos: Redwood Console gives per-route/model dashboards with token-level cost, traces, and error analysis — you can also export logs to your observability stack.
[06:58] Priya: Any gotchas for Private (on-prem)? Our security team will ask about upgrades, patching, and support SLAs.
[07:06] Lena: Private includes a managed control plane option or fully customer-managed. We provide upgrade tooling and an optional managed services engagement for patching and SLAs. We'll put those options in the follow-up.
[07:18] Marcus: Pricing high level — what does Dedicated commit look like? Monthly reserved GPU + overage?
[07:24] Lena: Typically a reserved monthly baseline with burst credits for overage and metered token costs for hosted. We'll send a sample TCO sheet for your expected volume.
[07:34] Priya: Ok want to circle back to model quality briefly — can you share short evals for our sample prompts? We'll send a subset.
[07:41] Carlos: Yes, please send top 50 prompts in English + top 20 in Spanish/German/Japanese. We'll run them on a few variants and return quality metrics and examples.
[07:52] Priya: We'll do that by Tuesday.
[07:55] Evan: One more — does Redwood support model composition / tool-chaining? We want the model to call a summarizer, then a Q&A tool, then the triage function.
[08:05] Carlos: We support orchestration patterns through our SDK and function-calling primitives. You can chain calls or use the pipeline features. We also have an examples repo for multi-step chains.
[08:18] Priya: Awesome. Any concerns about latency for multi-step chains?
[08:22] Carlos: Each step adds latency; we recommend batching where possible and using async background steps for non-blocking tasks. With Dedicated you can tune for lower tail latency.
[08:33] Lena: Alright I want to summarize next steps — we'll send pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted TCO, Carlos will share benchmark methodology and per-model perf sheets, and Skyward will share prompts and language priorities. We'll also schedule a 60-min SE deep-dive for benchmarks.
[08:48] Priya: Sounds good. Can we get the security pack (SOC2, data retention, KMS docs)?
[08:54] Lena: Yes will include security docs.
[08:57] Marcus: Thanks all. One last thing — any quick notes about migration if we start with Hosted and go to Dedicated? Is it mostly config or do we need to retrain?
[09:06] Carlos: Mostly config and routing; if you use the same model family and weights, you typically don't need retraining. You might re-tune prompts or quant settings. We'll help with rollout steps.
[09:18] Priya: Great. Thanks Lena and Carlos. We'll follow up with the prompt sets and a target pilot scope.
[09:25] Lena: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by Monday with the docs.

End of transcript.
